title: QCMI shell-telescoping boundary budget
question: Can the finite boundary information be decomposed into nonnegative QCMI shell increments whose telescoping l1 budget is auditable before seeking a uniform Gibbs complement and common-core transfer?
method: Build the exact zero-source oscillator chain on the manifest's 12 volume/cutoff systems and form normalized finite Gibbs matrices at every declared beta.
Enumerate both orientations of every admissible contiguous core--base-buffer--shell layout with core widths 1 and 2; add the shell sites one at a time and trace omitted exterior sites.
Compute each conditional mutual information increment delta_m=I(A:S_m|B S_1...S_{m-1}) and the cumulative I(A:S_1...S_m|B) from cached finite reduced spectra.
Check the QCMI chain rule to roundoff and retain the sum of increments as a finite l1 boundary budget, with no clipping of negative values.

Rebuild all aggregate fields in a non-importing independent lane, replace the interacting state by a product of one-site marginals as a hostile mutation, and compile scalar chain/budget identities in Lean R392.
finding: The primary lane passes 800/800 checks and the non-importing independent lane passes 6/6. The integrated verifier passes 21/21 with Lean R392 compiling over 12 systems, 44 base tripartitions and 264 shell rows. Every increment and cumulative QCMI value is nonnegative within tolerance; cumulative QCMI ranges from 4.991889248628922e-07 to 0.009400499834535836, the maximum l1 budget is 0.009400499834535836, and the maximum chain-rule residual is 1.7763568394002505e-15. The second shell maximum falls from 0.009400499834535836 to 0.0003382922777377395 for core width 1 and from 0.009319870748412562 to 0.0003364013516424791 for core width 2; a third one-site shell reaches 1.7918838214114885e-05. The product-of-one-site-marginals hostile mutation has maximum increment 1.7763568394002505e-15 while the interacting representative reaches 0.009270624713825448, so the mutation is caught.
decision_reason: R-392 adds a finite shell-accounting coordinate to R-391: QCMI increments are kept separately and their chain-rule sum gives an auditable boundary budget. Successive-shell suppression is visible on the declared grid, but no uniform shell modulus or Gibbs-complement control follows; the route remains an analytic target rather than a Q3LOCK or physical closure.

adversarial_review.check: The conditioning algebra includes exactly the previously added shell sites, so no commutation or translation assumption is introduced.
Negative increments and cumulative values are counted and rejected rather than clipped; both counts are zero.
The l1 budget retains the signed finite increments after positivity checks and is compared with the cumulative value through the explicit residual.
Left and right shell orderings are both enumerated and exterior sites are traced explicitly.
The second-shell suppression is kept as a finite profile and is not called exponential, cutoff-independent, or thermodynamic.
A product state that makes every shell increment vanish is compared with the interacting Gibbs state and caught above threshold.
The independent lane rebuilds the Hamiltonian, reductions, entropy and shell profiles without importing the primary module.
Uniform shell summability, Gibbs complement, common core, beta/eta independence, Cook/common-alpha, OS/KMS/GNS, gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A and Pre-A remain open.

next_action: Derive a cutoff-independent shell tail modulus for the actual Gibbs complement from the finite budget coordinate, then build the invariant common form-core transfer. If higher shells lose suppression under increasing cutoff, record the route-specific obstruction without promoting common alpha.
boundary: T0 claim-nonbearing finite QCMI shell-telescoping and boundary-budget stress only. It proves no uniform shell modulus, Gibbs complement theorem, cutoff/volume/source/shape bound, common core, beta/eta-independent topology, domain or Cook/common-alpha convergence, OS/KMS/GNS reconstruction, gap, continuum, C6, Sector-A or Pre-A result.
no_overclaim: Finite chain-rule closure and a finite l1 budget identify an accounting identity; they do not establish uniform summability or remove the spectral complement.
